subject: MedNova: embed flow gap analysis and next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Morgan <alyssa@mednova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: MedNova: embed flow gap analysis and next steps

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick thread to capture the things we heard, confirm priorities, and align on next steps so we all have the same playbook. I attached a short one-pager and the call recording.

Summary of what you described (pain & goal):
- Pain: current search/retrieval pipeline returns stale or incomplete candidate sets for triage use cases; relevance drops on notes >2k tokens and multi-document queries.
- Impact: clinicians are spending ~3x more time reviewing returned candidates and there are several missed findings in audits.
- Goal: reduce triage review time by 30% and improve precision@10 for critical queries by at least 20% within the pilot.

Product/technical constraints we heard:
- Data residency: logs and embeddings must be stored in their VPC for the pilot (MedNova legal & security).
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-query embedding+rerank path.
- EHR integration: onboarding team prefers server-side SDK with streaming responses to progressively show candidates in the UI.

Proposed Redwood approach (high level):
1) Embedding + rerank hybrid: generate coarse embeddings for retrieval, then run a lightweight reranker over top-K for precision.
2) Streaming + function-calling: use streaming SDK to emit partial candidate lists as they become available; expose a function-call hook for the UI to fetch expanded context on demand.
3) Private deployment option: offer Private (VPC) pilot to meet data residency and audit requirements.

Immediate asks / next steps (owner / ETA):
- Ben: send a short scope & pricing for a 6-week pilot w/ dedicated VPC nodes and up to 10M tokens/month (EOD 2026-11-30).
- Karthik: draft a technical runbook listing SDK changes (streaming API, function-call schema, structured output for candidate metadata) and a short integration checklist (EOD 2026-11-30).
- Alyssa: send SOC2 evidence doc and confirm 2-week window for engineering kickoff (you mentioned Dec 7–18) — please attach any onboarding contacts.

Open risks we flagged:
- If MedNova requires on-prem only (no VPC), timeline extends and costs increase — we should confirm during SOC review.
- Reranker compute: heavier models may need dedicated GPUs for low-latency; we'll provide a cost/latency matrix in the proposal.

Attachments: redwood-proposal-embedflow-v1.pdf (proposal sketch), discovery-call-20261128.mp3 (call recording).

If that aligns, I'll schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with Karthik and your eng lead. Thanks again — Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap, this is helpful. Confirming priorities & notes from our side:
- Primary: higher precision for diagnosis-related queries (these are the ones that cause the biggest review delays).
- Secondary: streaming is important — clinicians prefer to see initial candidates quickly and then refine.

A few clarifications:
- We can provide the SOC2 extract you requested (attached: mednova-soc2-extract.pdf). Ramon is looping in me as the PM; he'll own procurement approvals.
- For the VPC option, our infra team will need the network diagram and an IOPS estimate for the embedding store.

Timeline: the Dec 7–18 window works for an engineering kickoff. Procurement will need a formal statement of work and estimated cost for the first 3 months.

Quick ask for the proposal: include two pricing rows — (1) VPC pilot with reserved nodes and (2) hosted with strict retention controls — so we can compare TCO and security tradeoffs.

Thanks — Alyssa
